A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hamiltonian Flow Maps work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained material against the additions in v4.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of classical mechanical systems, MD17 molecules, and alanine dipeptide, including quantitative comparisons and extensive ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds Ac-Ala3-NHMe, coarse-grained protein simulations, trajectory-matching comparisons, and further diagnostic experiments.

M1.justification: The mean-flow objective, Algorithms 1–4, architectures in Appendix E, and coupled conservation filter remain unchanged. The new molecular applications use the existing framework; correcting 'endpoint-conditioned' to 'startpoint-conditioned' does not change the mathematical inputs or procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's classical systems, MD17 molecules, and alanine dipeptide, v4 evaluates MD22 Ac-Ala3-NHMe with a missing conformational mode and coarse-grained Chignolin and BBA proteins. It also adds paracetamol evaluations across temperatures from 300 to 700 K, substantially broadening molecular coverage and testing conditions.

E2.justification: Appendix G.14 adds an evaluated trajectory-matching training objective, following TrajCast/FlashMD, for paracetamol and Ac-Ala3-NHMe (Tables 19–20). This directly tests an important comparison absent from v1. Existing VV, MLFF, ScoreMD, and SchNet/NequIP timing comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols compare training objectives under force-evaluation budgets, generating trajectories at 0.5 fs and extracting state pairs separated by 7 fs. Protein evaluations introduce TICA projections and transition-probability comparisons; structural tables add HFM evaluation at 0.5 fs. The alanine total is corrected from 1 ms to 1 µs while ten 100 ns runs remain specified, indicating a reporting correction rather than demonstrated rerunning.

E4.justification: v4 adds temperature robustness tests, reference vibrational spectra investigating alanine instability, ethanol Lyapunov-time analysis, training-data-budget comparisons, and protein transition and individual-rollout analyses (G.10, G.12–G.17). These substantially extend v1's retained filter, timestep, sampling-distribution, and training-dynamics ablations.

E5.justification: G.5 explicitly identifies five distinct initial conditions for stability tests across all three thermostats, refining v1's replication description, which already reported five-run averages for related observables. The existing standard-deviation reporting remains; no increase in retained experiments' run counts or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Retained large-timestep values in Table 1 are unchanged, but new 0.5 fs results and substantial additional findings appear. For example, Table 19 reports paracetamol PMF errors of 0.129 for HFM versus 5.772 for trajectory matching at 256 force evaluations, while trajectory matching slightly wins at 85k. Table 21 newly shows Chignolin transition JSD increasing from 8.11e-4 at 25 fs to 5.11e-2 at 45 fs.

T1.justification: The consistency derivation, sufficiency argument in Appendix C, and constrained-conservation derivation in B.3 are retained. Norm-symbol and parenthesis corrections are not substantive mathematical changes. The new Lyapunov and transition analyses provide empirical evidence rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central claims: trajectory-free learning from instantaneous labels, joint instantaneous-force and finite-time prediction, and stable larger-timestep simulation at comparable computational cost. The expanded experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v1 identifies alanine instability near 10 fs without a specific vibrational explanation; v4 proposes cancellation errors when integration steps coincide with 10–11 fs hydrogen vibrations (G.12). It also attributes Chignolin population bias to ScoreMD distillation, interprets BBA discrepancies through trapped MLFF rollouts, and adds temperature-robustness and chaotic-error-propagation interpretations.

D1.justification: v1 links code; v4 additionally states availability of model weights and self-contained JAX/PyTorch notebooks. New Appendices F.6–F.7 document data selection, coarse-graining and ScoreMD relabeling, architecture settings, cutoffs, batch sizes, epochs, hardware, and training times for the added systems.

R1.justification: v4 explicitly credits Boffi et al.'s earlier flow-map framework, adds a PINN/Liouville-equation comparison, and cites additional relevant work such as Sabour et al. and the new datasets. The principal positioning remains intact; numerous publication-year and venue updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and appendix organization remain recognizable, with localized wording corrections, added experimental subsections, and 'Broader Impact' renamed 'Impact Statement.' Most existing methodological prose is retained; the added scientific content does not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 8 becomes a full-width composite retaining alanine results and adding protein panels. v4 adds substantial displays for missing-mode recovery, temperature tests, trajectory-matching comparisons, transition matrices, and protein rollouts. Spectral panels are redrawn, and structural-observable tables gain explicit headers and 0.5 fs columns.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses v1's missing direct trajectory-training comparison and limited molecular coverage, while adding diagnostics of robustness and temporal fidelity and expanding reproducibility information. These substantially strengthen the empirical foundation. Local weaknesses remain: Table 19 qualifies the claimed uniform HFM advantage, Table 20 and Figure 28 disagree on an Ac-Ala3-NHMe budget, and Table 21 limits the claimed kinetic accuracy at 45 fs. These issues constrain the strongest interpretations but do not outweigh the gains.
